## Where does a plant make food?

Mitochondria release energy from food, so a cell must first have food. Animals obtain food from their surroundings, but plants make theirs in the presence of sunlight. Plants do this in organelles called **plastids**.

<!-- STEP -->
## The green plastid

A **chloroplast** is a type of plastid. It holds a green pigment called **chlorophyll**, which absorbs sunlight. Like a mitochondrion, a chloroplast is surrounded by two membranes.

<!-- STEP -->
## Stroma and discs

Inside is a semi-fluid substance called the **stroma**. Within the stroma lie disc-shaped membrane structures that contain chlorophyll. During photosynthesis, these discs absorb the light energy.

<!-- STEP -->
## Where the sugar goes

The sugars made in photosynthesis are stored in the stroma, along with **starch granules**. Tap a name under the picture to light that part.
